title: Randomization-based confidence intervals for cluster randomized trials
headline: Open finding: exact nonzero-null validity requires a genuine null-removing transformation, a stronger condition than is stated explicitly in the paper's generic outcome-and-link formulation.

work.title: Randomization-based confidence intervals for cluster randomized trials

claims.label: Section 2.2.1 nonzero-null exactness
claims.gist: Fixing the observed treatment assignment as an offset while permuting a second assignment produces an exact level-alpha test for every nonzero null and hence a valid randomization confidence interval for generic outcome and link functions.
claims.statement: Fixing the observed treatment assignment as an offset while permuting a second assignment produces an exact level-alpha test for every nonzero null and hence a valid randomization confidence interval for generic outcome and link functions.
conditions: Cluster randomization under the Section 2.2.1 linked-mean model.
Nuisance parameters are treatment invariant as stated.
claims.quantifiers: Every null value theta_0 and generic outcome/link family described in Section 2.2.1.

result.summary: The printed generic nonzero-null exactness claim needs an additional genuine null-removing transformation condition. Without that condition, the eight-cluster finite-support NEF witness gives permutation p=1/35 at the true nonzero null and 95% coverage at most 0.83222784.
result.witness: On an event of probability (4/5)^8 the true nonzero null has permutation p=1/35 and is excluded, giving 95% coverage at most 0.83222784.
result.argument: The offset procedure keeps the observed assignment fixed inside the theta_0 x term while permuting a different assignment. That does not generally create an assignment-invariant null law. A genuine null-removing transformation does restore the required invariance. The finite witness lies inside the broader printed linked-mean model class but lacks such a transformation, so it demonstrates why the stronger condition is needed.
not_claimed: The theta_0=0 randomization test is invalid.
Models with a genuine null-removing transformation are invalid.
The responding author agreed that the published wording itself is defective.
result.repair_note: State explicitly that, for nonzero-null exactness, the assumed population model must admit a genuine null-removing transformation that makes the transformed outcomes assignment invariant under the null.

vor_check.detail: Source verification is at the canonical partial level; the record does not overstate Version of Record verification.

evidence.detail: A fresh separate-session hostile validation supports the stated finding; its scope and limits are summarized above.

author_response.covers: One author clarified that by 'correctly specified' the authors intended a model with a genuine null-removing transformation, and acknowledged that this can be more restrictive than some semiparametric models.
author_response.assessment: This accepts the substantive stronger condition identified in the technical note, but does not expressly concede that the published paper failed to state that restriction adequately. As Stated therefore narrows the finding from a false generic statement to a missing or hidden assumption.
